edits.value_json: 月 is interpreted as a pictograph of a half moon. A reported paleographic analysis says 月 and 夕 once shared a moon-shaped graph before later graphic specialization; Shang inscriptions attest 月 for both the moon and a calendar month, though the order of those uses is unresolved.

A reported paleographic analysis says 月 and 夕 once shared a moon-shaped graph; an interior dot did not initially distinguish them. It reports later graphic specialization associating the dotted form with 月 and the undotted form with 夕. The date and mechanism of this differentiation remain unresolved.

The current Chinese dictionary records 月 with the meaning ‘each month’. Shang inscriptions also attest its use for a calendar month, associated with the moon’s waxing and waning cycle; the chronology relative to the moon sense is unresolved.
